items.title: Houthis launch first missile attack on Israel as U.S. Marines reach Middle East

featured_image.name: U.S. to Deploy Marines to Middle East. Here's What They Could Be ...

items.description:
The USS Tripoli and roughly 2,500 Marines arrived in the Middle East on Friday as Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen launched their first missile attack on Israel since the war began, opening a new front in a rapidly expanding regional conflict now one month old.

U.S. Central Command announced Saturday that the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group and the embarked 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit reached its area of responsibility on March 27, carrying approximately 3,500 sailors and Marines along with strike fighter aircraft and amphibious assault assets. The America-class amphibious assault ship had departed its homeport of Sasebo, Japan, earlier this month after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth approved a CENTCOM request for reinforcements.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: WHO says nine paramedics killed in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israel Killed Over a Dozen Lebanese Paramedics in Three Days ...

items.description:
The World Health Organization said Saturday that nine paramedics were killed and seven others wounded in five separate attacks on healthcare teams in southern Lebanon, bringing the total number of health workers killed since the Israeli military escalation began on March 2 to 51.[1][2]

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus detailed the strikes in a post on X, saying medics were hit while on duty in five villages. In Zoutar al-Sharqiya, five health workers were killed and two injured, one critically. Two more were killed and three wounded in Kfar Tibnit. One paramedic died in each of Ghandouriyeh and Jezzine, while two were wounded in Kfar Dajjal.[2][3]

"The repeated attacks on health care are severely disrupting the delivery of services in southern Lebanon," Tedros wrote, adding that "the only way to end these tragedies is to end attacks on health care, NOW".[2]

items.description: The United Nations sounded urgent alarms on Friday over Lebanon's rapidly deteriorating humanitarian situation, with UNHCR warning the country is on the brink of a "humanitarian catastrophe" as Israeli strikes and ground operations enter their fourth week. More than 1.2 million people have been displaced since fighting escalated on March 2, including over 370,000 children uprooted at a rate of 19,000 per day, according to UN officials briefing reporters in Geneva.[1][2][3]

items.title: Bahrain says it intercepted 559 Iranian missiles and drones

featured_image.name: Bahrain air defense systems intercept over 150 missiles and 360 drones

items.description: Bahrain's Defense Force announced Saturday that its air defense systems have intercepted and destroyed a cumulative total of 174 missiles and 385 drones since Iranian attacks on the Gulf kingdom began on February 28. The latest figures mark a sharp increase from earlier this week, when Bahrain reported intercepting 154 missiles and 362 drones, underscoring the relentless pace of strikes nearly a month into the conflict.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Debris from intercepted Iranian missile injures 5 in Abu Dhabi

featured_image.name: UAE considers striking Iranian missile sites as regional war spreads

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates intercepted six ballistic missiles and nine unmanned aerial vehicles launched from Iran on March 27, the UAE Ministry of Defence announced, as the Gulf nation endures near-daily attacks that have now stretched into a second month.[1][2]

The interception brought the UAE's cumulative defense tally since the start of the conflict to 378 ballistic missiles, 15 cruise missiles, and 1,835 drones destroyed, according to the ministry. On Saturday morning, falling debris from another intercepted missile sparked two fires in the Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi, injuring five Indian nationals, according to CNN-News18.[2][3][1]
